name: fig1_thermal_margin_3d
title: Cooling margin of a Joule-heated measurement over operating temperature and heat load
question: How much documented cooling power is left (or missing) at each operating temperature and heat load, and does the Lean verdict agree with the sign of that margin?
model: M = P_cool(T_doc) - Q with Q = I^2 R; joule_heating_vs_cooling_power passes iff M >= 0. T_doc is the highest documented, installed, non-estimate cooling-power temperature not above T_op (serialize.resolve_slots).
data: 1020 Lean checks (check_batch, 0.9 s), 3 configurations x 17 T_op x 20 Q, same grid as fig_thermal_feasibility_3d; P_cool is the rhs Lean used, asserted equal to the sourced catalog value; margin sign vs verdict inconsistencies: 0; 360 points have no usable cooling power (margin undefined). paper/data/fig1_thermal_margin_3d.json.
caption: Height and colour give the cooling margin P_cool(T_doc) - Q (symmetric log, linear within 1 nW), with P_cool the sourced cooling power the Lean checker used; marker shape is the Lean verdict. Circles (met) lie above the zero plane and crosses (not met) below it. Where no documented, non-estimate cooling power applies (below the lowest documented temperature; OptistatDry TLEX at 4.2-5 K, documented only as an estimate) the margin is undefined, Lean answers Need more information, and those points are drawn as triangles on the floor rather than given an invented margin.

name: fig_mechanical_clearance_3d
title: 3D mechanical compatibility: sample size vs documented clearance
question: Does a sample of a given width/diameter and height fit the documented sample space, and how much clearance remains?
model: Requirements sample.diameter.max >= D and sample.height.max >= H decided by the Lean checker; clearance = documented limit - requested size
caption: Mechanical compatibility in three dimensions. A synthetic experiment family requests a sample of width/diameter D and height H (12 x 12 grid; user_entered requirements sample.diameter.max >= D and sample.height.max >= H). Markers are verdicts of the compiled Lean 4 checker (864 checks over 6 configurations); surfaces are the binding remaining clearance min(D_max - D, H_max - H) computed from manufacturer-documented limits, zero contour in black. Lean verdicts and the sign of the sourced clearance agree on 720 of 720 documented points. Bluefors LD400 (renamed LD450) with side-loading ports (LD400sl) and High-Density Wiring in one side-loading port lists both size keys with unknown values, so every request is Need more information, never a pass. Across the catalog only 67 of 220 configurations document a numeric diameter and height limit; sample.width.max is numeric for 6 and sample.length.max for 3, so full width x length x height footprints cannot be checked for most configurations.
notes: Diameter is the lateral limit because sample.width.max is numeric for very few configurations; the fit of a rectangular sample's diagonal in a circular bore is not modeled. The clearance surface is arithmetic on sourced values, not a verdict.

name: fig_lean_z3_performance
title: Lean 4 and Z3 runtime vs problem size
question: How do verification (Lean) and solver (Z3) runtimes scale with the number of experiment x configuration pairs?
model: Wall-clock timing (time.perf_counter) of lean_runner.check_batch, smt.evaluate, smt.rank_alternatives and scripts/build_grid.py on the same pairs.
caption: Measured runtime of the Lean 4 checker (decides every verdict) and Z3 (explains and ranks) against problem size on a 32-CPU machine. Medians of 5 runs (3 runs for Z3 at 1000 pairs); bars span min to max. Lean check_batch in one process: 5000 pairs in 4.83 s (0.97 ms/pair). Z3 evaluate, serial: 1000 pairs in 7.0 s (7.0 ms/pair). Full grid (44,880 pairs, scripts/build_grid.py, 24 worker processes, including serialisation and database writes): median 51 s over 3 runs. Z3 was not run on the full grid and no extrapolation is drawn.

name: fig_cross_industry_heatmap
title: Cross-industry compatibility heatmap (full catalog)
question: Which cryogenic configurations can run which experiments, across 20 industries?
model: Lean 4 checker verdicts (cryolean grid table); no re-evaluation, no Z3
caption: Every cell is a verdict of the compiled Lean 4 checker for one experiment-configuration pair of the full catalog (204 experiments, 220 configurations, 44,880 stored pairs; grid built 2026-11-01T06:41:05+00:00). Rows are grouped by the experiment's industry (catalog order). The catalog assigns no industry to configurations, so columns are grouped by each configuration's home industry, defined here as the industry in which it has the most REQUIREMENTS_MET pairs (ties go to the earlier industry), with 11 configurations that meet no experiment in a final block; within a block columns are sorted by equipment family. Black lines mark industry block boundaries. Totals: 3,118 met, 11,463 need more information, 30,299 not met. Right panel: verdict shares and counts (met/need info/not met) per experiment industry.
notes: Column home industry is a grouping derived from Lean MET counts, not catalog data. Pairs absent from grid: 0.
